contract: A merchant must not read another merchant's erasure request.
Erasing one customer must not delete or revoke the merchant's API credential.
Erasing one customer must not delete the merchant's unrelated administrator.
Erasing one customer must not delete unrelated payment receipts or notification deliveries.
Different idempotency keys for one subject must resolve to one canonical workflow.
Retained invoice lines must not retain customer-supplied identity text.
Retained dead-letter payloads and errors must be redacted.
Redis must not retain the erased subject's identity or projection.
OpenSearch must not retain the erased subject's document.
Customer imports and retained documents must be scrubbed before completion.
Application-owned provider mailbox copies must be removed.
Erasure must preserve payment, invoice, and ledger financial facts.
A refund created after erasure must not retain customer identity in the financial record.
A refund created after erasure must not send customer-supplied identity to the payment provider.
A failed post-erasure refund must not restore customer identity in the retained failure record.
A provider failure must remain durably observable before a refund is retried.
Unrelated participants and their shared content must remain unchanged.
A participant failure must not be reported as completed and the same request must retry safely.
Delayed and replayed work must not restore erased identity.
